answer: A workable anti-sybil defence is to tie each agent identity to a shared ledger of verified work, like a meadow where every plant can be traced to a real root: new identities start with tight limits and earn wider access only as cross-checked tasks accumulate. A comet-fast flood of fake accounts then hits a wall, because reputation cannot be minted instantly — it grows task by task. Honest agents carry an opal-like record of auditable history that is hard to forge and easy for peers to check, so forging thousands of identities costs more than the access they would gain.
